chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from Ja'far ibn Sama'ah from Aban from Fadl ibn 'Abd al-Malik from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

The young virgin girl who is under the guardianship of her parents is not asked for her permission when her father intends to marry her off; he is more considerate for her. And as for the mature woman (thayyib), she is asked for her permission even if she is under the guardianship of her parents when they intend to marry her off.

key_terms.الثَّيِّبُ: Mature woman (previously married or of age)
key_terms.بَيْنَ أَبَوَيْهَا: Under the guardianship of her parents

ai.seo_question: What is the difference in marriage consent rules between a virgin and a mature woman in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the fiqh of marital consent, distinguishing between the 'bikr' (virgin) whose father's permission suffices as a sign of respect, and the 'thayyib' (mature/divorced widow) whose explicit agreement is mandatory. It reflects the Shia scholarly view that while paternal authority exists for young virgins, it does not override the autonomy of a woman who has previously experienced marriage, ensuring her active participation in the contract.
